points.t: A red, moist, sore rash under the breasts, in the groin, armpits or abdominal folds, especially with obesity, diabetes or incontinence.
Skin-on-skin friction plus trapped sweat causes maceration; yeast and bacteria colonise secondarily.
Dry and separate the folds (cotton, moisture-wicking textiles), barrier products, short mild steroid; treat confirmed candida or erythrasma specifically.
Flexural psoriasis, extramammary Paget disease, and erythrasma or tinea treated as ‘simple intertrigo’.

points: Erythema, itch/burn, moist/macerated skin, fissures in crease depth, peeling.
Sites: inframammary, axillae, groin, abdominal apron, natal cleft, neck, finger/toe webs.

cards.name: Irritant intertrigo
cards.clue: Symmetrical fold erythema, moist, ± mild peripheral scale

cards.name: Tinea cruris
cards.clue: Annular plaque, **raised active border**, central clearing; often asymmetrical

cards.name: Erythrasma
cards.clue: Red-brown patch, minimal scale, little itch

cards.name: Seborrhoeic dermatitis
cards.clue: Ill-defined salmon-pink thin patches in axilla/groin

cards.name: Hailey–Hailey (if relevant)
cards.clue: Painful erosions, fissures, flaccid blisters in axilla/groin; familial

items.t: Rash that fails to clear in one fold, especially in an older adult: biopsy for **extramammary Paget disease**.
Spreading redness, pain and fever: cellulitis.
Repeated ‘intertrigo’ that relapses as soon as treatment stops: think **inverse psoriasis** (see the [psoriasis](condition:psoriasis) page).

pearls.t: KOH negative ≠ “never fungal” — sampling error and mixed pictures exist; re-test if course atypical.
Combination clotrimazole–HC / similar: pragmatic in primary care but reassess if no clear infection signs and no improvement.
Counsel that **prevention** (dryness) beats endless cream cycles.
